questions.question: How do cubes control data in OneStream?

options.A: They control how data is calculated and translated based on the dimensions assigned to the cube
options.B: They control how data is stored and consolidated based on the dimensions assigned to the cube
options.C: They control how data is stored, calculated, translated, and consolidated based on the dimensions assigned to the cube
options.D: They control only how data is displayed in reports

questions.explanation: C is correct: the dimensions assigned to a cube tell the data how to be controlled across all four functions — storing, calculating, translating, and consolidating. A is incorrect — it omits storing and consolidating. B is incorrect — it omits calculating and translating. D is incorrect — display formatting is a reporting concern, not a core cube control function.

questions.question: Where is the Default Currency assigned within a cube in OneStream?

options.A: Cube Dimensions tab > Default Scenario Type
options.B: Cube Properties tab > FX Rates section
options.C: Cube References tab > Cube for Referenced Entity Dimensions section

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Default Currency for a cube is defined by accessing the Cube Properties tab, then the FX Rates section. A is incorrect — the Cube Dimensions tab handles dimension assignment by Scenario Type, not currency. C is incorrect — Cube References governs referenced entity dimensions between cubes. D is incorrect — Application Properties governs application-wide settings like the Global POV, not a single cube's default currency.

questions.question: Which two items ARE included in an extracted OneStream application zip file? (Select 2.)
questions.explanation: C and D are correct: an extracted application zip file contains Application Artifacts, which include items like Cube Views, Form Templates, and Metadata. A and B are incorrect — FX Rates and Data are explicitly NOT part of an application artifact extract; they are handled through separate mechanisms (FX Rates via the Cube Properties FX Rates section, Data via Data Management/import-export processes).

questions.question: An administrator needs to enable a dimension for a cube so that data can be imported into that dimension. Which property on the cube's Integration tab should be set to True?
questions.explanation: A is correct: setting the Enabled property to True on the cube's Integration tab allows data to be imported to that dimension. B is incorrect — Profile Active controls whether a Workflow Profile is active, not dimension import eligibility. C and D are incorrect — these are not real OneStream cube Integration tab properties.

questions.question: On a cube's Integration tab, which font color indicates that a dimension is enabled?
questions.explanation: D is correct: an enabled dimension displays in black font on the cube Integration tab, distinguishing it from disabled dimensions. A, B, and C are incorrect — gray, blue, and red are used for other states (disabled, hyperlink/reference, or error indicators respectively), not the enabled state. Note: this question's source screenshot did not reveal a confirmed answer; the correct answer was determined independently based on the standard OneStream UI convention for enabled vs. disabled dimension styling.

questions.question: Which sections on the cube Integration tab are used to load additional detail to the stage that will be excluded from storage in the cube itself?

options.B: Label dimensions, Attribute dimensions, and Attribute Value dimensions
options.C: Cube dimensions, Attribute dimensions, and Attribute Value dimensions

questions.explanation: B is correct: Label dimensions, Attribute dimensions, and Attribute Value dimensions are all used to bring additional detail into the stage that is excluded from cube storage. A, C, and D are incorrect — each either includes Cube dimensions (which ARE stored in the cube) or omits one of the three correct stage-only dimension types.

questions.question: Where can calculation processes (Can Calculate, Can Translate, Can Consolidate) be enabled within a Cube View?
questions.explanation: A is correct: setting the Can Calculate, Can Translate, and Can Consolidate properties to True under General settings > Common enables these functions directly within the Cube View data explorer grid. B, C, and D are incorrect — Report and Header Overrides govern layout and presentation, not calculation permissions, and Data Explorer > Settings is not the location for these properties.

questions.subtopic: Cube View Configuration — Substitution Variable Prefixes
questions.question: Which prefix is used in substitution variables to pull values from the Cube View POV?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the CV prefix pulls values from the Cube View's own POV. B is incorrect — WF pulls from the user's Workflow POV instead (a related but distinct substitution variable prefix). A and D are incorrect — MF is not a standard POV-source prefix in this context, and POV itself is not the prefix syntax used.

questions.subtopic: Cube View Configuration — Substitution Variable Prefixes
questions.question: Which prefix is used in substitution variables to pull values from a user's Workflow POV?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the WF prefix pulls values from the user's current Workflow POV. C is incorrect — CV pulls from the Cube View's own POV instead, a distinct source. A and D are incorrect — neither is the correct prefix syntax for this purpose.

questions.question: Which variable type is used to create dynamic headers, footers, and page captions in Cube Views?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Substitution Variables are used to build dynamic headers, footers, and page captions that update based on the current POV context. B, C, and D are incorrect — these are not the standard OneStream mechanism for this specific purpose.

questions.question: Which cell color indicates that a cell is drillable in a Cube View?
questions.explanation: B is correct: blue cells in a Cube View indicate that the cell is drillable, allowing the user to view underlying detail. A, C, and D are incorrect — these colors are reserved for other cell states (such as errors, locked cells, or non-drillable data).

questions.question: What does the Global Point of View (POV) in Application Properties include?

options.B: Company Name and Logo, Number Format, and Currency Filter
options.C: Cube View Profiles and Dashboard Profiles

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Global POV in Application Properties includes settings such as Company Name and Logo, Number Format, and Currency Filter. A is incorrect — Default Currency and FX Rates are configured at the cube level (Cube Properties > FX Rates), not in the Global POV. C and D are incorrect — these are unrelated configuration areas.

questions.subtopic: Application Properties — Currency Filter by Scenario Type
questions.question: An administrator wants to add a currency that can be used across ALL Scenario Types. Where should they configure this?

options.A: Application Properties > General tab > Default Scenario Type > Currency Filter
options.B: Application Properties > General tab > Budget Scenario Type > Currency Filter
options.C: Application Properties > General tab > Actual Scenario Type > Currency Filter

questions.explanation: A is correct: adjusting the Currency Filter property under the Default Scenario Type in Application Properties applies the currency across all Scenario Types, since other Scenario Types inherit from the Default unless overridden. B and C are incorrect — adjusting a specific Scenario Type (Budget or Actual) only affects that type, not all of them. D is incorrect — Cube Properties > FX Rates governs a cube's default currency, not which currencies are available application-wide.

questions.question: Where can an administrator find the property to Lock After Certify within OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: within Application > Tools > Application Properties, an authorized user can configure a workflow to lock automatically after the certify step has been completed for a specific Scenario Type. A is incorrect — Workflow Profiles configure the workflow structure itself, not this application-wide locking behavior. C and D are incorrect — these are unrelated configuration areas.
